macros.name: bst
macros.doc: \bst {⟨bibstyle name⟩} typesets the name of a BibTEX bibliography style.

macros.name: class
macros.doc: \class {⟨class name⟩} typesets the name of a LaTeX class.

macros.name: cname
macros.doc: \cname {⟨command name⟩} is like \cs but its argument is evaluated and prefixed with a backslash character.

macros.name: code
macros.doc: \code {⟨verbatim text⟩} and |⟨verbatim text⟩| typeset short pieces of code verbatim.

macros.name: env
macros.doc: \env {⟨environment name⟩} typesets the name of a LaTeX environment.

macros.name: ext
macros.doc: \ext {⟨extension⟩} typesets the name of a disk file extension.

macros.name: file
macros.doc: \file {⟨file name⟩} typesets the name of a disk file.

macros.name: marg
macros.doc: \marg {⟨mandatory argument⟩} typesets a mandatory argument, and \oarg {⟨optional argument⟩} typesets an optional argument.

macros.name: oarg
macros.doc: \marg {⟨mandatory argument⟩} typesets a mandatory argument, and \oarg {⟨optional argument⟩} typesets an optional argument.

macros.name: option
macros.doc: \option {⟨option name⟩} typesets the name of a package or class option.

macros.name: package
macros.doc: \package {⟨package name⟩} typesets the name of a LaTeX package.

macros.name: program
macros.doc: \program {⟨program name⟩} typesets the name of a computer program.

macros.name: todo
macros.doc: The \todo {⟨text⟩} command and the todoenv environment are analogous to \caveat and warning, but they typeset paragraphs of a task “to do”.

macros.name: typeset
macros.doc: \typeset {⟨text⟩} typesets ⟨text⟩ in a normal way, but indicates by boxing that the contents are an example of how some piece of code actually appears.

envs.name: bothexample
envs.doc: The bothexample and bothexample* environments typeset their contents two times, side by side.

envs.name: todoenv
envs.doc: The \todo {⟨text⟩} command and the todoenv environment are analogous to \caveat and warning, but they typeset paragraphs of a task “to do”.

envs.name: typesetexample
envs.doc: The typesetexample environment typesets its contents like \typeset except they are set off in their own indented block element instead of being boxed.
